title: As a developer, the API parses complex real-world PDFs — multi-column layouts, headers, footers, footnotes — into clean, correctly ordered content
As an ML engineer, parsed output preserves document hierarchy — headings, sections, reading order — so downstream LLMs see structure, not soup
As an ML engineer, figures and charts are extracted or described (VLM summaries, image crops) with positions traceable back to the source page
As an ML engineer, the vendor publishes reproducible accuracy benchmarks and I can run my own evals before committing
As a data engineer, complex tables — merged cells, nested headers, multi-page spans — come out as faithful HTML/markdown structure
As a data engineer, I turn extracted tables into typed rows/JSON I can load into a database without manual cleanup
As a developer, scanned and photographed documents OCR accurately — skewed pages, stamps, low quality scans included
As a developer, handwritten fields and annotations are recognized and extracted, flagged with confidence when uncertain
As a developer, non-English documents — including CJK and right-to-left scripts — parse with the same fidelity as English
As a developer, I supply a JSON schema and get back validated structured fields extracted from the document
As an AI-native user, every extracted field carries provenance — page number, bounding box, source snippet — so agents can cite and humans can verify
As a data engineer, extractions carry calibrated confidence scores with a human-in-the-loop review path for low-confidence fields
As a data engineer, multi-document packets are classified and split automatically — one upload, per-document results
As a developer, one API handles my whole document mix — PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML, images, email — without per-format plumbing
As a data engineer, thousand-page documents and multi-gigabyte files process reliably without timeouts or silent truncation
As an AI-native user, output comes pre-chunked for RAG — semantic boundaries, metadata, embedding-ready segments — not a wall of text
As an AI-native user, I get clean markdown/JSON designed for LLM consumption, with noise like repeated headers and page furniture stripped
As a developer, long parses run as async jobs with status polling and completion webhooks, so my pipeline never blocks
As a data engineer, I push high-volume batches — millions of pages — with documented rate limits and predictable throughput
As a developer, a fast synchronous mode returns results in seconds for interactive apps, with latency documented per mode
As a developer, official typed SDKs for Python and TypeScript cover the full API — parse, extract, jobs — with sensible defaults
As a developer, I drag a document into a web playground and see parse/extract results before writing any code
As a data engineer, I can run the extraction stack in my own VPC or fully self-hosted when documents can't leave my infrastructure
As a data engineer, uploaded documents get zero-retention handling with SOC 2 and HIPAA options, so I can process contracts and medical records
